# Install Grafana Alloy

{{< docs/video id="TaNNEjKCh8Q" align="right" start="79" end="137" >}}

In this milestone, you install Grafana Alloy on your system.
Alloy is available for multiple operating systems and deployment environments, making it easy to integrate into your infrastructure.

{{< /docs/video >}}

The steps in this milestone install Alloy as a system service.
You can also install Alloy as a standalone binary.
Refer to [Run Grafana Alloy as a standalone binary](/docs/alloy/latest/set-up/install/binary/) for the procedure.

To install Alloy, complete the following steps:

1. Download the appropriate Grafana Alloy package for your operating system from the [Grafana Alloy releases page](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/releases).

1. Install Grafana Alloy using your system's package manager or installation method. If the method you are using isn't listed, refer to [Install Grafana Alloy](/docs/alloy/latest/set-up/install/).
   {{< tabs >}}
   {{< tab-content name="Ubuntu and Debian" >}}

   1. Navigate to the [latest release](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/releases/latest) on GitHub.
   1. Scroll down to the **Assets** section.
   1. Download the DEB package file that matches your system architecture.
   1. Install the package:

      ```shell
      sudo dpkg -i alloy-*.deb
      ```

   {{< /tab-content >}}
   {{< tab-content name="RHEL, CentOS, and Fedora" >}}

   1. Navigate to the [latest release](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/releases/latest) on GitHub.
   1. Scroll down to the **Assets** section.
   1. Download the RPM package file that matches your system architecture.
   1. Install the package:

      ```shell
      sudo rpm -i alloy-*.rpm
      ```

   {{< /tab-content >}}

   {{< tab-content name="macOS" >}}

   You can install Alloy on macOS with Homebrew.

   1. Add the Grafana Homebrew tap:

      ```sh
      brew tap grafana/grafana
      ```

   1. Install Alloy:

      ```sh
      brew install grafana/grafana/alloy
      ```

   {{< /tab-content >}}

   {{< tab-content name="Docker" >}}

   1. Pull the latest Grafana Alloy Docker image:

      ```sh
      docker pull grafana/alloy:latest
      ```

   1. Create and save an Alloy configuration file on your computer, for example:
      ```alloy
      logging {
         level  = "info"
         format = "logfmt"
      }
      ```

   1. Run the Grafana Alloy Docker container, replacing `<CONFIG_FILE_PATH>`:

      ```sh
      docker run \
         -v <CONFIG_FILE_PATH>:/etc/alloy/config.alloy \
         -p 12345:12345 \
         -p 4318:4318 \
         -p 4317:4317 \
         --name grafana-alloy \
         grafana/alloy:latest \
            run --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345 --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data \
            /etc/alloy/config.alloy
      ```

   {{< /tab-content >}}

   {{< tab-content name="Windows" >}}

   1. Navigate to the [latest release](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/releases/latest) on GitHub.
   1. Scroll down to the **Assets** section.
   1. Download the file called `alloy-installer-windows-amd64.exe.zip`.
   1. Extract the downloaded file.
   1. Double-click on `alloy-installer-windows-amd64.exe` to install Alloy.

   {{< /tab-content >}}
   {{< /tabs >}}

## Run Alloy and verify the installation

Alloy should run as a system service or inside a Docker container.
Use these steps to confirm Alloy is installed correctly.

1. Run Alloy and verify the service status is running, if installed as a system service:

   {{< tabs >}}
   {{< tab-content name="Linux" >}}

   1. Start Alloy:

      ```sh
      sudo systemctl start alloy
      ```

   1. Verify Alloy is running:

      ```sh
      sudo systemctl status alloy
      ```

   {{< /tab-content >}}

   {{< tab-content name="macOS" >}}

   1. Start Alloy:

      ```sh
      brew services start grafana/grafana/alloy
      ```

   1. Verify Alloy is running:

      ```sh
      brew services info grafana/grafana/alloy
      ```


   {{< /tab-content >}}

   {{< tab-content name="Windows" >}}

   1. Open the **Windows Services** manager:

      1. Right click on the Start Menu and select Run.
      1. Type: `services.msc` and click **OK**.

   1. Scroll down to find the Alloy service and verify that the **Status** is **Running**.

   {{< /tab-content >}}
   {{< /tabs >}}


   If you are using **Docker** or just want an extra sanity check that Alloy is running successfully, navigate to [`http://localhost:12345`](http://localhost:12345) and make sure the Alloy UI loads without error.
